title: Order Management Schedule: Hold Duration Limits and Informed Consent Settings
content:
Laboratory Test Orders may be held before collection (an information hold) or after accessioning (a testing hold). Each service class sets the longest each hold may last, and whether signed patient informed consent is required.

| Service class | Information hold maximum (calendar days) | Testing hold maximum (calendar days) | Signed informed consent required before testing | Consent valid for collection (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Routine Clinical Testing | 14 | 3 | No | 0 |
| Specialty Clinical Testing | 14 | 7 | No | 0 |
| Esoteric Reference Testing | 14 | 7 | No | 0 |
| Molecular Infectious Disease Testing | 7 | 3 | No | 0 |
| Clinical Toxicology Testing | 14 | 14 | No | 0 |
| Anatomic Pathology & Cytology | 30 | 30 | No | 0 |
| Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing | 30 | 45 | Yes | 90 |

## Column meanings

- **Information hold maximum** — the calendar days a pre-collection information hold may last before the laboratory cancels the order.
- **Testing hold maximum** — the calendar days a specimen may stay on testing hold before the laboratory cancels the order.
- **Informed consent required** — whether a signed patient informed-consent form is required before testing.
- **Consent valid for collection** — the calendar days a signed informed consent remains valid for collection; 0 where consent is not required.

## Observations

- Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing is the only class requiring informed consent, and its consent stays valid for 90 calendar days. It also allows the longest testing hold (45 days).
- Molecular Infectious Disease Testing has the shortest information hold (7 days); Routine Clinical Testing and Molecular Infectious Disease Testing share the shortest testing hold (3 days).
